assembly_notes:
The root is always `frame`, a single welded CadQuery solid. It is built in three passes:
(1) union the family's plates, base structure, bosses, bracket and — when web_relief is
enclosed_guard_shell — the shroud; (2) cut the family's own openings (bolt slots, web
windows, the guard fairlead); (3) cut every rotating member's swept envelope out of it.
Pass 3 is not a safety net, it is the design: it produces the drum bore, the reduction-gear
window, the guard's spindle relief and the annular pawl slot as real geometry, and it is the
reason `allow_overlap` is never called anywhere in this template.

Every rotating member is authored in its own local frame with its rotation axis on local +X
through the local origin, and is placed by `mate_axes(provider, consumer)` +
`register_interface_mate`, so the frame family can put that axis on world +X (horizontal
cheek families) or world +Z (vertical_capstan_deck) without any member being re-authored.
The only non-axis articulation is removable_spindle_socket's withdrawal prismatic, whose
parent is the drum rather than the frame.

Cross-slot sizing runs one way, host last: line_takeup and ratchet_pawl fix the drum's radial
envelope, drive_coupling adds either nothing (direct/removable) or an offset pinion that
reaches further toward the mounting plane than the drum does, and only then does
frame_family derive `axis_lift_m` (or `pedestal_h_m` for the capstan), `plate_reach_m` and the
two plate stations. The axial stack runs the same way: the drum's disc list fixes
`drum_u_min_m`/`drum_u_max_m`, the plates go outboard of those, and the crank plane goes
outboard of the plates, which is how a full-circle crank sweep can never reach the frame.

Contacts are real fits, not interpenetrations: every bore is `shaft + bore_clearance_m` with
`bore_clearance_m <= 0.0012`, so it stays inside the 1 mm gap the baseline QC counts as
support; the gear mesh is a tangent pair separated by `gear_backlash_m` and asserted with the
source's own `expect_contact` tolerance; and the pawl nose reaches half a tooth depth inside
the tip circle at its engaged pose.

derived.expression: max(flange_radius_m, ratchet_tip_r_m, takeup_outer_r_m, drum_gear_tip_r_m if reduction else 0.0)
derived.name: max_drum_radius_m
derived.rationale: The drum's largest rotating radius depends on the active ratchet_pawl, line_takeup and drive_coupling choices, so the host cannot size itself from its own parameters.

derived.name: rotating_reach_m
derived.rationale: Adding the offset pinion's downward reach is the specific correction this rebuild makes: without it a reduction seed puts the pinion under the base plate.

derived.name: axis_lift_m
derived.rationale: Horizontal families lift the drum axis; the capstan spends the same clearance axially through pedestal_h_m.

derived.name: pedestal_h_m
derived.rationale: vertical_capstan_deck only: how high the pedestal must raise the capstan so the lowest rotating disc clears the deck top. This is the fix for the source capstan's ratchet gear being buried in its deck disc.

derived.expression: max(plate_reach_ratio * rotating_reach_m, pawl_ring_r_m + pawl_boss_r_m + 0.004, gear_center_distance_m + pinion_bore_boss_r_m + 0.004)
derived.name: plate_reach_m
derived.rationale: The plate has to be big enough to carry the pawl bracket and, when a reduction is active, the offset pinion bore.

derived.name: ratchet_u_m
derived.rationale: The ratchet ring sits just outboard of the +u flange, matching 002's ratchet-outboard-of-the-cheek stack and 003's gear-beside-the-flange stack.

derived.expression: ratchet_u_m + ratchet_thickness_m / 2 + (0.0 if not reduction else plate_gap_m + gear_thickness_m + (stage_gap_m + gear_thickness_m if two_speed else 0.0))
derived.name: drum_u_max_m
derived.rationale: The most +u rotating disc, which decides where the far bearing plate goes and therefore where the crank plane can be.

derived.name: drum_u_min_m
derived.rationale: The self-tailing crown extends the drum on the -u side, which is why the source fork narrows the spool widths to make room.

derived.expression: plate_u_far_m + plate_thickness_m / 2 + crank_gap_m for horizontal families; drum_u_max_m + crank_gap_m + coupler_len_m for vertical_capstan_deck
derived.name: crank_u_m
derived.rationale: The crank arm plane is always axially outboard of every frame face, which is how the sources keep a full-circle crank sweep from ever touching the frame (003: crank arm at x=0.073 against a cheek that ends at 0.065).

derived.expression: one cylinder per rotating band: barrel, both flanges, ratchet ring, each reduction gear, the crown or the wound spool, the spindle, each pinion and its shaft, plus one annulus per pawl
derived.name: envelope_cut_list
derived.rationale: Every rotating member's swept volume is boolean-subtracted from the frame solid after it is welded, so the bore, the gear window and the pawl slot are real openings. MECHANICAL_PRIORS 4 and 7 require exactly this, and it is what makes enclosed_guard_shell combinable with every drive coupling instead of excluded.

derived.name: pawl_slot_outer_r_m
derived.rationale: Outer radius of the annular slot cut for each pawl's full swing; the long release lever needs a much bigger one than the compact lobe.

derived.name: pawl_slot_inner_r_m
derived.rationale: Inner radius of that slot, so the pivot pin itself survives the cut and still carries the pawl.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: pawl_half_w_m is derived as clamp(0.40 * pawl_ring_r_m * pawl_pitch_rad, 0.0045, 0.014), so adjacent pawl bodies keep at least a fifth of the pivot pitch between them at every N and the frame's pawl slot is one merged annulus rather than N separate pockets. N is capped at 3 because a fourth pivot at the same span would push pawl_half_w_m under 4.5 mm, thinner than the 0.0030-0.0048 pivot pin it has to carry; the pool's own upper bound is also 3. Every value is source-backed: 1 (pawl_count_single_pawl), 2 (pawl_count_dual_pawl), 3 (pawl_count_triple_pawl).
multiplicities.name: pawl_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: pivot i sits on the ring at angle pi/2 + (i - (N-1)/2) * pawl_pitch_rad measured in the (r1, r2) radial plane, i.e. regular steps centred on the top of the ratchet, which is 001's triple fork (_pawl_layout: PAWL_RING_ANGLES = 125 deg + 20 deg * i on one ring) generalised and recentred; 002's dual fork is the same rule at N=2.

candidates.evidence: Horizontal drum axis carried in a symmetric clevis: one base flange plus two cheeks extruded from a seven-point triangular side profile, joined by a transverse tie into one welded solid, with both shaft passages cut as true clearance bores, four elongated bolt slots in the flange and the pawl spindle unioned into the right cheek. Bearing collars and bolt heads are separate hardware visuals at the cheek stations.

dimensions.bore: cut as a true clearance, 003 L100-L107

candidates.name: folded_twin_cheek
candidates.notes: Two identical cheeks extruded from one tapered silhouette, standing on a base flange and tied together by a transverse cylinder, all unioned into one welded solid before the rotating envelopes are cut. Intra-part welds are free (collision is only computed between parts), so this stays one visual.

parameters.name: base_plate_h_m
parameters.rationale: Thickness of the grounded mounting structure the frame stands on. Pool: 0.004 (003 L58 base_t), 0.020 (002 L241 mounting_foot), 0.016 (001 L231 base_bridge), 0.008 (capstan L56 base_t). Its top face is the plane every rotating envelope has to clear.

parameters.name: base_clearance_m
parameters.rationale: Radial (horizontal families) or axial (capstan) gap left between the lowest rotating element and the top of the mounting structure. Pool: 002 leaves 9 mm (flange bottom 0.033 vs foot top 0.024), 003 leaves 46 mm (gear bottom 0.050 vs flange top 0.004). Directly feeds axis_lift_m, which is the derivation the legacy template did not have.

parameters.name: plate_thickness_m
parameters.rationale: Thickness of one bearing plate / cheek / deck. Pool: 0.004 (003 L59 side_t), 0.008 (002 L54 front cheek extrude), 0.0045 (001 L186 side plate), 0.008 (capstan L56 deck).

parameters.name: plate_reach_ratio
parameters.rationale: Bearing-plate silhouette radius as a multiple of rotating_reach_m, before the cross-slot floors in binding drive_and_pawl_size_the_frame apply. Pool: 003's cheek profile peaks 0.062 above a 0.048 gear tip (1.29); 002's cheek peaks 0.058 above a 0.057 ratchet tip (1.02).

parameters.name: flange_clearance_m
parameters.rationale: Axial gap between a drum disc face and the neighbouring frame plate face. Source 002 L564-L573 asserts exactly this as expect_gap(front_flange, front_cheek, min_gap=0.001, max_gap=0.004).

parameters.name: running_clearance_m
parameters.rationale: Radial and axial margin added to every rotating member's swept envelope before it is boolean-cut out of the frame solid. This is what turns 'the gear must not touch the plate' into real geometry; source 001 achieves the same result by narrowing the base bridge until the 74 mm toothed flange runs outboard of it (L228-L235).

parameters.name: bore_clearance_m
parameters.rationale: Radial clearance of a frame bore around the shaft that passes through it. Source 003 L100-L107 cuts both shaft passages as 'true clearances, not hidden intersections'; 002 L56-L62 cuts a 0.0165 shaft clearance for a 0.008 spindle. Kept well under 1 mm so the bore still counts as support under the baseline QC gap rule, and floored at 0.6 mm so the fit survives tessellation on both sides (the template meshes at a 0.18 mm sagitta, so a bore and its shaft together can lose about 0.36 mm of clearance to chords).

parameters.name: cheek_taper_ratio
parameters.rationale: Half-width of the cheek silhouette at its crown as a fraction of plate_reach_m, which is what gives 003 its triangular profile. Source 003 L65-L73: the profile is 0.166 long at the base and 0.060 wide at the top, i.e. about 0.36.

parameters.name: tie_radius_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the transverse tie cylinder that makes the two cheeks one load path. Source 003 L91-L97: 0.0045 over a 0.122 span.

parameters.name: rotating_reach_m
parameters.rationale: The single largest distance any rotating member reaches away from the drum axis toward the mounting plane, taking the active drive coupling into account.

parameters.name: axis_lift_m
parameters.rationale: Height of the drum axis above the mounting plane for the three horizontal families. Deriving it from rotating_reach_m rather than from the drum flange alone is what keeps the ratchet ring, the drum gear and the offset pinion out of the base plate at every seed.

parameters.expression: max(plate_reach_ratio * rotating_reach_m, pawl_ring_r_m + pawl_boss_r_m + 0.004, gear_center_distance_m + pinion_bore_boss_r_m + 0.004 if reduction else 0.0)
parameters.name: plate_reach_m
parameters.rationale: Bearing-plate silhouette radius. Floored so the plate actually reaches the pawl pivot ring and, when a reduction is active, the offset pinion bore.

parameters.name: plate_u_near_m
parameters.rationale: Axial station of the near bearing plate: outboard of the most -u drum disc, so no plate ever shares an axial band with a rotating disc.

parameters.name: plate_u_far_m
parameters.rationale: Axial station of the far bearing plate / pedestal, outboard of the most +u drum disc (the ratchet ring, or the outermost reduction gear).

parameters.name: plate_gap_m
parameters.rationale: The plate stand-off must exceed the envelope clearance, otherwise cutting the rotating bands out of the frame would eat into the bearing plates themselves.

Asymmetric part profile, one plate instead of two, and the drum overhangs the front plate instead of sitting between two identical cheeks.

parameters.name: web_boss_ratio
parameters.rationale: Outer radius of the raised bearing boss as a multiple of the bore radius. Pool: 002 L252-L260 front bushing 0.0167 outer on a 0.0085 bore (1.96); 001 L210-L215 bearing collar 0.025 outer on a 0.0183 bore (1.37).

candidates.evidence: Five circular lightening windows cut clean through the web while a continuous perimeter, the bearing web and diagonal load paths around both shafts are retained, so the frame reads as an open-cheek reel with the drum visible through it.
candidates.name: windowed_web
candidates.notes: Circular lightening windows cut clean through the web on a ring between the bore boss and the silhouette edge, leaving a continuous perimeter.

parameters.name: window_count
parameters.rationale: Number of windows cut through each web. Source open_cheek_reel L92-L107 cuts five.

parameters.name: window_radius_ratio
parameters.rationale: Window radius as a fraction of plate_reach_m. Source open_cheek_reel L93-L97 uses 0.014-0.019 radii on a 0.062-reach cheek, i.e. 0.23-0.31 of the reach; scaled down here because plate_reach_m is measured from the axis.

candidates.evidence: The opposite treatment: a curved guard shell is unioned around the drum between the bearing stations, with a broad side fairlead window cut out so the line can leave, a widened bearing ring under it and a spindle clearance re-cut through the ring after the union — so the winch reads as an enclosed reel with the drum hidden behind a shroud.
candidates.name: enclosed_guard_shell
candidates.notes: A curved shroud is unioned around the drum between the bearing stations, with one angular fairlead window cut out for the line. The shell is then re-cut by every rotating envelope, which is exactly the correction the enclosed source fork makes when it re-cuts its spindle clearance after unioning the ring (L108-L112).

parameters.name: guard_thickness_m
parameters.rationale: Wall thickness of the guard shell. Source enclosed fork L100-L103: 0.066 - 0.0585 = 0.0075.

parameters.name: guard_window_span_rad
parameters.rationale: Angular span of the fairlead window cut out of the shroud so the line can leave. Source enclosed fork L105-L111 cuts a 0.052 x 0.046 box out of a 0.066 shell, which subtends roughly 0.9 rad.

candidates.evidence: No gears: a bored coupling sleeve plus a solid outboard stub captures the projecting drum spindle and the crank turns coaxially with the drum, so the crank joint origin sits on the main shaft and every crank station moves outboard by the coupler length.

dimensions.crank_plane: crank_u_m, always outboard of the frame's outermost face

candidates.name: direct_socket_drive
candidates.notes: No gears at all: a bored coupling sleeve plus a solid outboard stub captures the projecting drum spindle, so the crank's rotation axis IS the drum axis and pinion_low_reach_m is zero. Joint: continuous, parent frame, coaxial with the drum axis.

parameters.name: crank_reach_m
parameters.rationale: Radial distance from the drive axis to the grip axle. Pool: 0.059 (003 L322-L348, hypot(0.031, 0.052)), 0.117 (002 L24-L25 HANDLE_END), 0.123 (001 L338-L345 crank outline tip), 0.120 (capstan L280-L294).

parameters.name: crank_arm_width_m
parameters.rationale: Width of the crank arm across the sweep plane. Pool: 0.017 (003 L324 Box), 0.009 (002 L133-L149 arm half-width 0.0045 doubled), 0.018 (capstan L281).

parameters.name: crank_gap_m
parameters.rationale: Axial gap from the outermost frame face to the crank arm plane, i.e. how far outboard the sweeping crank is kept. Pool: 003 puts the crank arm at x=0.073 with the cheek ending at 0.065 (0.008); the direct-drive fork moves it to 0.084 (0.019).

parameters.name: coupler_len_m
parameters.rationale: Axial length of the bored coupling sleeve that grips the drum spindle. Source direct_drive fork L296-L300: a 0.0053 tube plus a 0.012 stub.

parameters.name: coupler_wall_m
parameters.rationale: Wall thickness of that sleeve. Source direct_drive fork L296-L299: 0.010 - 0.003 = 0.007 outer wall over the spindle.

parameters.name: pinion_low_reach_m
parameters.rationale: No offset shaft, so the drum's own envelope is the only thing axis_lift_m has to clear.

parameters.name: coupler_bore_r_m
parameters.rationale: The sleeve is bored to a running fit on the spindle rather than interpenetrating it; under 1 mm it still counts as support.

candidates.evidence: One matched 3:1 spur pair emitted from an indexed stage loop — a 30-tooth gear on the drum and a 10-tooth pinion on a second shaft offset from the drum axis — with the crank on the pinion shaft and the mesh asserted by a contact check rather than a volumetric overlap.

dimensions.crank_plane: crank_u_m, always outboard of the frame's outermost face

parameters.name: drum_gear_teeth

parameters.name: pinion_angle_rad
parameters.rationale: Angle of the offset pinion axis measured in the radial plane from the +r1 direction, negative meaning below the drum axis. Source 003 L21-L24: the drive shaft sits at dy=+0.048, dz=-0.043 from the main shaft, i.e. -0.73 rad.

parameters.name: gear_backlash_m
parameters.rationale: Gap left between the two tip circles. Sized against the contact tolerance the source itself asserts the mesh with (0.0012 in 003 L547-L554, 0.0020 in the two-speed fork).

parameters.name: gear_thickness_m
parameters.rationale: Axial thickness of a gear ring. Pool: 0.009 (003 SpurGear width 9 mm), 0.007 (two-speed fork width 7 mm).

parameters.name: gear_module_m
parameters.rationale: Module chosen so the drum gear comes out the same size as the ratchet ring it sits beside, which is the relation source 003 has (48 mm gear tip against a 46 mm flange).

parameters.name: drum_gear_tip_r_m
parameters.rationale: Standard tip radius m*(n/2 + 1), as source 003's SpurGear(module=3, teeth=30) gives 0.048.

parameters.name: pinion_tip_r_m
parameters.rationale: Same law for the pinion; source 003's 10-tooth module-3 pinion gives 0.018.

parameters.name: gear_center_distance_m
parameters.rationale: Tip circles are separated by a positive backlash instead of interleaved. Source 003 L547-L554 asserts the mesh as expect_contact(contact_tol=0.0012) named 'reduction gears are closely meshed WITHOUT overlap', and the two-speed fork widens that tolerance to 2 mm; a tangent mesh satisfies the same assertion and, unlike an interleaved one, cannot be broken by motion QC turning the two independent continuous joints to different angles.

parameters.name: pinion_low_reach_m
parameters.rationale: How far below the drum axis the offset pinion reaches. This term is the reason axis_lift_m cannot be derived from the drum alone: in source 003 it is 0.061 against a 0.048 gear tip.

parameters.name: pinion_bore_boss_r_m
parameters.rationale: Boss radius the frame plate needs around the pinion bore; feeds the plate_reach_m floor.

parameters.name: pinion_shaft_r_m
parameters.rationale: Source 003 L291 runs a 0.0046 shaft under an 0.018 pinion.

parameters.rationale: Total angular span across which the N pawl pivots are spread on their ring, centred on the +r2 (top) direction. Pool: 002's dual fork puts its two pivots about 1.22 rad apart; 001's triple fork uses regular 0.349 rad steps, i.e. 0.70 rad for three.

parameters.name: lobe_radius_ratio
parameters.rationale: Radius of the round pivot lobe as a fraction of pawl_ring_gap_m. Source 002 L176-L181: a 0.009 lobe against a 0.0153 ring gap, i.e. 0.59.

parameters.name: pawl_ring_r_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the pivot ring every pawl sits on, stated generally by 001's triple fork as PAWL_RING_RADIUS.

parameters.name: pawl_pitch_rad
parameters.rationale: Regular angular step between adjacent pivots; 001's triple fork uses a constant 20 deg step from 125 deg.

parameters.name: pawl_half_w_m
parameters.rationale: Tangential half-width of a pawl body, derived from the pivot pitch so adjacent pawls cannot touch at any N. This is the host-capacity rule for the multiplicity.

parameters.name: pawl_bore_r_m
parameters.rationale: The pawl bore is a running clearance on the pin, so the pin and the pawl never share material; sources 002 and 003 both needed allow_overlap here and this removes it.

parameters.name: pawl_boss_r_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the frame's pivot boss/bracket around the pin. Source 002 L65-L71: a 0.009 boss on a 0.0038 pin; 001 L254-L259: a 0.022 x 0.034 bracket on a 0.0045 pin.

parameters.name: pawl_engaged_tip_r_m

parameters.name: pawl_outer_reach_m
parameters.rationale: How far the body reaches outward from the pivot; sets the outer radius of the swept envelope cut out of the frame.
